pathway.name: First unprovoked seizure (adult)
pathway.population: Adults after a first unprovoked seizure
pathway.summary: Emergency assessment, EEG and MRI, first seizure clinic or neurologist review, and an antiseizure medicine for those at high recurrence risk.

steps.label: Levetiracetam 500 mg
steps.note: Started if recurrence risk is high

pathway.name: Epilepsy, new diagnosis (adult)
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed epilepsy
pathway.summary: Neurologist diagnosis with EEG and MRI, monotherapy for most, and a minority with emergency presentations or admissions in the first year.

pathway.name: Drug-resistant focal epilepsy (surgical evaluation)
pathway.population: Adults with focal epilepsy despite two appropriate medicines
pathway.summary: Epilepsy centre review, video EEG monitoring admission, MRI and neuropsychology, polytherapy, and resective surgery for a minority.

pathway.name: Epilepsy, new diagnosis (child)
pathway.population: Children aged 2 to 12 with newly diagnosed epilepsy
pathway.summary: Paediatric neurology assessment, sleep-deprived EEG, MRI for focal epilepsy, liquid antiseizure medicine, rescue medicine, and ED visits for some.

steps.label: Midazolam oromucosal (child dose)
steps.note: Rescue medicine for home and school

pathway.name: Childhood absence epilepsy
pathway.population: Children aged 4 to 10 with typical absence seizures
pathway.summary: EEG with hyperventilation confirms the diagnosis, ethosuximide or valproate, and paediatric neurology follow-up.

pathway.name: Infantile spasms (West syndrome)
pathway.population: Infants presenting with epileptic spasms
pathway.summary: Urgent admission with prolonged EEG, MRI and genetic testing, first-line prednisolone or vigabatrin, close follow-up and developmental review.

pathway.name: Dravet syndrome
pathway.population: Children with Dravet syndrome on established treatment
pathway.summary: Specialist epilepsy care with high-cost add-on medicines (stiripentol, fenfluramine, cannabidiol), rescue medicine, frequent ED visits and admissions for prolonged seizures.

pathway.name: Simple febrile seizure
pathway.population: Children aged 6 months to 5 years with a first simple febrile seizure
pathway.summary: Emergency assessment and short admission for some, then GP follow-up. No investigations or medicine for most.

pathway.name: Convulsive status epilepticus (adult)
pathway.population: Adults presenting in convulsive status epilepticus
pathway.summary: Emergency treatment, intensive care with ventilation for a quarter, admission and investigation of the cause, then neurology follow-up.

pathway.name: Episodic migraine
pathway.population: Adults with episodic migraine seen in general practice
pathway.summary: GP diagnosis and management with triptans, a preventive for about a third, neurology referral for a minority and occasional ED visits.

pathway.name: Chronic migraine
pathway.population: Adults with chronic migraine (15 or more headache days a month) under a neurologist
pathway.summary: Neurology care with oral preventives, botulinum toxin injections and CGRP monoclonal antibodies for those who qualify, plus acute treatment.

steps.label: Botulinum toxin injections for chronic migraine

pathway.name: Cluster headache
pathway.population: Adults with episodic cluster headache
pathway.summary: Neurologist diagnosis, brain imaging, verapamil prevention, steroid bridging during bouts, and acute treatment.

pathway.name: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
pathway.population: Adults, mostly women, with newly diagnosed IIH
pathway.summary: MRI with venography, lumbar puncture, acetazolamide, neurology and ophthalmology follow-up, and surgery for the few with threatened vision.

steps.label: Shunt or venous sinus stenting admission

pathway.name: Acute ischaemic stroke
pathway.population: Adults admitted with acute ischaemic stroke to a public hospital
pathway.summary: Emergency imaging and reperfusion (thrombolysis inside the admission price, clot retrieval for about one in seven), stroke unit care, rehabilitation and secondary prevention.

pathway.name: Transient ischaemic attack
pathway.population: Adults presenting with a TIA
pathway.summary: Emergency or rapid-access clinic assessment, carotid and cardiac investigations, secondary prevention, and carotid surgery for a few.

steps.label: CT angiography of neck and brain vessels

pathway.name: Intracerebral haemorrhage
pathway.population: Adults admitted with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
pathway.summary: Emergency care, stroke unit or intensive care admission, neurosurgery for a minority, rehabilitation and blood pressure control.

pathway.name: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage
pathway.population: Adults with aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage
pathway.summary: Emergency diagnosis, aneurysm securing by coiling or clipping with intensive care, long admission, then imaging follow-up and rehabilitation.

steps.label: Cranial intervention admission, major complexity
steps.note: Coiling or clipping with ICU care

pathway.name: Relapsing multiple sclerosis, new diagnosis
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed relapsing-remitting MS
pathway.summary: MRI of brain and spine, lumbar puncture for some, a high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy for most, infusion day visits and MS clinic follow-up.

pathway.name: Primary progressive multiple sclerosis
pathway.population: Adults with primary progressive MS
pathway.summary: Ocrelizumab for eligible patients, annual MRI, rehabilitation and spasticity management, and admission for complications.

pathway.name: Generalised myasthenia gravis
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed generalised myasthenia gravis
pathway.summary: Neurology diagnosis with antibodies and neurophysiology, pyridostigmine, steroids and a steroid-sparing agent, immunoglobulin for exacerbations, and crisis care for a few.

steps.label: Repetitive nerve stimulation or single fibre EMG
Intravenous immunoglobulin course (2 g/kg)
steps.note: Funded through the National Blood Authority, not the PBS

price.ref: Estimate: about 140 g at about $70/g national blood price; check against National Blood Authority price list

pathway.name: Guillain-Barré syndrome
pathway.population: Adults admitted with Guillain-Barré syndrome
pathway.summary: Emergency admission, immunoglobulin for most, intensive care with ventilation for some, then rehabilitation.

steps.label: Peripheral nerve disorder admission, major complexity
Intravenous immunoglobulin course (2 g/kg)
steps.note: Funded through the National Blood Authority, not the PBS

price.ref: Estimate: about 140 g at about $70/g national blood price; check against National Blood Authority price list

pathway.name: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
pathway.population: Adults with CIDP on maintenance treatment
pathway.summary: Nerve conduction studies, maintenance immunoglobulin infusions every three to four weeks for most, steroids for some, and neurology review.

price.ref: Estimate: about 70 g at about $70/g national blood price

pathway.name: Autoimmune encephalitis
pathway.population: Adults admitted with autoimmune encephalitis
pathway.summary: Long admission with MRI, EEG and lumbar puncture, steroids and immunoglobulin, intensive care for some, then rehabilitation and neuropsychology.

steps.label: Intravenous immunoglobulin course (2 g/kg)
steps.note: Funded through the National Blood Authority, not the PBS

price.ref: Estimate: about 140 g at about $70/g national blood price; check against National Blood Authority price list

pathway.name: Parkinson's disease, new diagnosis
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed Parkinson's disease
pathway.summary: Neurologist diagnosis, levodopa for most and a dopamine agonist or MAO-B inhibitor for some, GP care planning and allied health.

pathway.name: Advanced Parkinson's disease (device-aided therapy)
pathway.population: Adults with advanced Parkinson's disease and motor fluctuations
pathway.summary: Movement disorder clinic care and device-aided therapy: deep brain stimulation, subcutaneous foslevodopa infusion, intestinal levodopa gel or apomorphine.

pathway.name: Essential tremor
pathway.population: Adults referred with essential tremor
pathway.summary: Neurologist diagnosis, propranolol or similar for those troubled by tremor, and review.

pathway.name: Cervical dystonia
pathway.population: Adults with cervical dystonia treated with botulinum toxin
pathway.summary: Botulinum toxin injections every three months, with toxin supplied under Section 100, and neurology review.

pathway.name: Tourette syndrome (child)
pathway.population: Children with Tourette syndrome
pathway.summary: Paediatric assessment, behavioural therapy, and medicine for the minority with impairing tics.

pathway.name: Huntington's disease
pathway.population: Adults with manifest Huntington's disease
pathway.summary: Specialist and psychiatric care, chorea treatment with tetrabenazine, allied health, and admissions for complications.

pathway.name: Restless legs syndrome
pathway.population: Adults with moderate to severe restless legs syndrome
pathway.summary: GP diagnosis, iron studies, dopamine agonist or gabapentinoid treatment, and neurology referral for a few.

pathway.name: Motor neurone disease
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed motor neurone disease
pathway.summary: Diagnosis with neurophysiology and MRI, riluzole, multidisciplinary MND clinic care, and admissions for respiratory and feeding problems.

pathway.name: Spinal muscular atrophy (child on treatment)
pathway.population: Children with SMA on established disease-modifying treatment
pathway.summary: Neuromuscular clinic care with nusinersen intrathecal maintenance doses or daily risdiplam, respiratory and orthopaedic surveillance.

steps.label: Risdiplam oral solution (Section 100)
steps.note: One bottle lasts about two weeks

name: Spinal muscular atrophy, infant identified by newborn screening

pathway.name: Spinal muscular atrophy, infant identified by newborn screening
pathway.population: Infants with SMA found on newborn screening
pathway.summary: Rapid confirmation, then one-off onasemnogene gene therapy for most eligible infants or nusinersen loading, with close neuromuscular follow-up.

steps.label: Nusinersen 12 mg (loading year)
steps.note: Four loading doses then every 4 months

pathway.name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (child)
pathway.population: Boys aged 5 to 12 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy
pathway.summary: Neuromuscular clinic care, daily steroids, cardiac and respiratory surveillance, and allied health.

pathway.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
pathway.population: Adults and adolescents with suspected CMT
pathway.summary: Neurologist assessment, nerve conduction studies, genetic testing, orthotics and podiatry, and foot surgery for a few.

steps.label: Orthoses
steps.note: Usually paid by patient or NDIS

price.ref: Estimate: ankle-foot orthoses; not covered by Medicare

pathway.name: Myotonic dystrophy type 1
pathway.population: Adults with myotonic dystrophy type 1
pathway.summary: Genetic confirmation, cardiac conduction surveillance with ECG and Holter, pacing for some, and neuromuscular review.

pathway.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
pathway.population: Adults with carpal tunnel syndrome referred for investigation
pathway.summary: Nerve conduction studies, splinting or steroid injection, and carpal tunnel release for those with moderate to severe disease.

pathway.name: Bell's palsy
pathway.population: Adults with acute Bell's palsy
pathway.summary: GP or ED diagnosis, early prednisolone, eye protection, and neurology review for atypical cases.

pathway.name: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy
pathway.population: Adults with diabetes and painful peripheral neuropathy
pathway.summary: GP management, nerve conduction studies for atypical cases, and neuropathic pain medicine.

pathway.name: Alzheimer's disease dementia (mild to moderate)
pathway.population: Older adults with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease
pathway.summary: GP and memory clinic care, brain imaging, cholinesterase inhibitor or memantine, and admissions for complications or delirium.

pathway.name: Mild cognitive impairment
pathway.population: Older adults presenting with memory concerns
pathway.summary: GP screening and bloods, brain imaging, memory clinic or specialist assessment, and neuropsychology for some.

pathway.name: Cerebral palsy (child)
pathway.population: Children with spastic cerebral palsy, GMFCS II to IV
pathway.summary: Paediatric rehabilitation clinic care, botulinum toxin for spasticity, allied health, hip surveillance and orthopaedic surgery for some.

pathway.name: ADHD (child, new diagnosis)
pathway.population: Children aged 6 to 12 with newly diagnosed ADHD
pathway.summary: Paediatrician assessment and diagnosis, stimulant medicine for most, and regular reviews to adjust dose.

pathway.name: Autism assessment and first year (child)
pathway.population: Children aged 2 to 6 assessed for autism
pathway.summary: Paediatrician and psychology assessment, genetic tests for some, Medicare-funded speech pathology and occupational therapy, and sleep medicine for a few.

pathway.name: Global developmental delay
pathway.population: Children under 5 with global developmental delay
pathway.summary: Developmental assessment, genetic testing (microarray, fragile X, exome for some), MRI for selected children, and early allied health.

pathway.name: Neonatal hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (cooled)
pathway.population: Term newborns treated with therapeutic hypothermia
pathway.summary: NICU admission with cooling, EEG monitoring and MRI (inside the admission), then neurodevelopmental follow-up and early intervention.

steps.label: NICU admission, intermediate complexity
steps.note: Cooling, ventilation, EEG and MRI included

pathway.name: Concussion (child or adolescent)
pathway.population: Children and adolescents with sport-related concussion
pathway.summary: Emergency assessment, short admission for a few, and GP-led graded return to school and sport.

name: Moderate to severe traumatic brain injury

pathway.name: Moderate to severe traumatic brain injury
pathway.population: Adults admitted with moderate to severe TBI
pathway.summary: Emergency care, intensive care and neurosurgery for some, long admission, then rehabilitation and neuropsychology.

pathway.name: Bacterial meningitis (adult)
pathway.population: Adults admitted with bacterial meningitis
pathway.summary: Emergency treatment, admission for intravenous antibiotics, intensive care for some, and hearing and neurology follow-up.

steps.label: Nervous system infection admission, major complexity
Nervous system infection admission, minor complexity

pathway.name: Glioblastoma
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma
pathway.summary: Maximal safe resection, chemoradiotherapy with temozolomide, adjuvant temozolomide, MRI surveillance, and admissions for complications.

price.ref: Estimate: MBS radiation oncology items for a 30-fraction course; replace with itemised MBS fees

pathway.name: Functional neurological disorder
pathway.population: Adults with functional motor symptoms or seizures
pathway.summary: Neurologist diagnosis with investigations to exclude other causes, ED presentations, and physiotherapy and psychological therapy.

pathway.name: Narcolepsy
pathway.population: Adults with suspected narcolepsy
pathway.summary: Sleep physician assessment, overnight sleep study with multiple sleep latency test, and wake-promoting medicine.

pathway.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
pathway.population: Adults presenting with positional vertigo
pathway.summary: GP or ED diagnosis with a repositioning manoeuvre, and specialist or vestibular physiotherapy referral for recurrent cases.

steps.label: Vestibular physiotherapy
steps.note: Private, partly covered by health insurance
